passages.arabic: فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا ﴿٥﴾ إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا ﴿٦﴾
passages.translation: For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.
passages.explanation: The promise is repeated twice, as if to settle a worried heart. A hard week of deadlines is not the whole story; relief is described as arriving with the difficulty, not only after it.
passages.reflection: What is one small sign of ease you can notice in this busy week?

passages.arabic: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُم بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ ۗ أَلَا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ
passages.translation: Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.
passages.explanation: When thoughts keep circling, this verse points to remembrance as a place where the heart can settle. Many students pair a few quiet moments of dhikr with slow breathing before sleep or an exam.
passages.reflection: Which thought has been replaying most often, and what would it feel like to set it down for five minutes?

passages.arabic: وَلَا تَهِنُوا وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا وَأَنتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
passages.translation: So do not weaken and do not grieve, and you will be superior if you are [true] believers.
passages.explanation: This verse was revealed after a painful setback, encouraging believers not to give up. A low grade or a slow week does not decide who you are or where you can go.
passages.reflection: What is the smallest next step you could take today, even if motivation is low?

passages.arabic: إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا
passages.translation: ...when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us."
passages.explanation: These words were spoken by the Prophet ﷺ to his companion while hiding in a cave during the Hijrah, far from home. Even in a crowded cafeteria where you feel unseen, you are not truly alone.
passages.reflection: Who is one person you could message today, simply to say hello?

passages.translation: And made your sleep [a means for] rest.
passages.explanation: Sleep is listed among the blessings we are given. Resting is not laziness; it is part of how we are made, and it helps both study and mood.
passages.reflection: What is one thing you could change tonight to protect your sleep?

passages.arabic: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
passages.translation: Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity.
passages.explanation: When everything feels like too much, this verse reminds us that our capacity is known. It can be a gentle invitation to rest and to ask for help, rather than push harder.
passages.reflection: What is one thing you could put down or ask help with this week?

passages.arabic: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ
passages.translation: And when My servants ask you, [O Muhammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.
passages.explanation: Allah describes Himself as near to the one who calls. Reaching out in dua can sit alongside reaching out to people: a friend, family member, teacher or counsellor.
passages.reflection: Who is one trusted person you could talk to if things feel heavy?

passages.arabic: وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ مَا هُوَ شِفَاءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
passages.translation: And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers...
passages.explanation: Many people find comfort and meaning in time spent with the Quran. That comfort can go hand in hand with care from doctors and counsellors; one does not replace the other.
passages.reflection: When did reading or listening to the Quran last bring you calm?
